doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: Marrero's rhythm style and George Guesnon's teaching
summary: Marrero describes himself as a solid band banjoist rather than a soloist, recalls a fine rhythm section, and praises George Guesnon, whom his brother taught.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When you're stroking a banjo, I mean, you see I really think that I play different from a fellow. See I play my own way, I don't try to cover kept behind nobody. See? When I play, I give everybody a heavy compliment and cold. I'm not too much of a soloist, very little. Good band banjo. Solid beat. Well yes.

Yes I do. And we had, I'll tell you, we had one of the best rhythm sessions they had. George Moods, George Moods, yeah. Elton Pointer, and Joe Watkins on the drums. Yeah, we had one of the best rhythm sessions I think they had on. Yeah. Well see my banjo playing is cold and heavy comp. And when they tell me to get off, I get off. That's where I do it now. That's where the people, these people take a light to my playing because I play it different from everybody. I'm trying to get up there and try to play solo, banjo solos all night, you see. Because I can't do that. I mean, I could do it some things. But I don't play banjo solos. At that time, you be doing this. People think you're crazy. Keep it up. And exercise your wrist. Just roll around, make it up. Yeah. That George Gino. See George Gino? That's a son of a gun man. I wish I had to wrist George Gino ahead. And George Gino, my brother taught George Gino. Is that right? Sure my brother taught George Gino. I used to go around there and sit around there and I used to teach all them guys too. And my brother didn't have time. But George Gino can teach me now. And I really wish I'd know half of what George Gino know. I'm pretty good. Well, I'm telling you the truth. I wish I'd know half of what George Gino knows. He's a really good man you play. And guitar player too. George Gino is a wonderful guy.
